author: Stannis
text_post: I honestly see myself mirrored in a lot of your experiences. While I’m not handsome by any stretch and I only had girls make an explicit pass at me twice (early teens and then mid-teens), I have had women initiate me or display clear sexual interest in me on multiple occasions, which relative to the extent of my hermitage is not infrequent (whether it was genuine or not is a different question). I’m absolutely positive if it weren’t for the unfortunate constellation of my upbringing and resulting social maladaption I would have had non-monetary sex already and then some. Most people active in the incel communities seem to operate under the assumption that a woman will literally force herself on you if you are in the upper echelon looks-wise. Which might or might not be true, I wouldn’t know. But it seems unlikely to me, particularly in a diurnal context. In clubs and bars, maybe. I think a fitting analogy would be being invited to a job interview instead of it being offered outright. There is a strong interest there and the high likelihood that you will get if you take some initiative and don’t act like a socially inept retard with an entire graveyard in the closet. Women operate in that liminal sphere of the unspoken and try to maintain plausible deniability at all times. By and large their fear of losing face is bigger than their fear of losing out. And I guess the same would apply what’s commonly referred to as ‘mentalcels’. It’s funny that you mention Narcissus. There seems to be an additional layer to the story involving Echo. It seems to highlight the complete inability of communication between a woman and a shy man. Both communicate passively and show no proactivity in the dynamic between them. It really mirrors a lot of my past experiences with women. A lot of implications (like the chameleon effect in case of echo) and indicators of interest, nothing overt, and then a sudden gesture of affection which would blindside me and to which I would react highly adversely. And I think this incongruence between looks and behaviour is even more off-putting to women than an ugly guy acting meek, as that’s what they expect of him. If you still a certain amount of physical appeal and act in a way that suggests that can’t find any social footing their assumption that that’s a symptom of an even worse problem than merely being ugly. It makes them wary of you. On the one hand they are drawn to you on a primal level whereas they can simply ignore ugly guys, on the other however you constitute a great risk to them as they can’t assess whether getting involved with you will be a social drawback to them. Women are extremely drawn to good-looking men but are also very practically minded and will do anything to safeguard their social capital.

author: silvereagle
text_post: Stannis, yes concur 100%. Attractive women and girls have in my youth, and even in my thirties, been instinctively warm to me, shown clear interest; yet my obvious lack of esteem in my teens, and later just incongruous behaviour, lack of assertiveness, and strangeness, have frightened them off. As you say, a handsome, desirable man behaving like a weird nerd who, in the latter case, understandably has no confidence, throws them off. It doesn't compute. So they shrug, and move on.  On Narcissus and Echo, yes it is a very profound myth within a myth, and clearly has multiple meanings. Why Narcissus and Echo have featured in art and literature (including the psychological literature), it resonates. Also in my memoir, there is a chapter - a gloss on my inadvertent rejection of a string of beauties - entitled 'Narcissus spurns the nymphs...' Why the story of Narcissus and Echo sends shivers down my spine. There is so much to the myth of Narcissus, not least because there are several versions. On women literally throwing themselves on men, you are right of course, women and girls don't do this, because as you put it, they don't need to do it. Obviously they literally throw themselves onto famous rock stars and actors, but naturally we are speaking about 99.99% of men here and not the experiences of Lenny Kravitz and Zach Efron. It was in hindsight terribly inevitable, but of course you don't see it coming. As you stay Stannis, you are always blindsided. In other words, it's a lot like life. It is life. Every single opportunity I had with females, from my teens through to a few weeks ago! (after years of nothing at all, I mentioned the case of Tess recently), without exception, came from left-field. I never saw it coming and always responded like a gibbering idiot who had the day off from the mental hospital. I never learned because my self-esteem was so low, I thought it would never happen again. And then it would happen again, always out of the blue, from nowhere. And I was always thus blindsided, and I panicked every single time. And of course there is the complete lack of experience with girls, I mean total, not even a single real kiss, that serves to reinforce my frozen mental state with women, in a kind of feedback loop.
